source: T-6A Techniques and Procedures Manual (I.N. T-6A 02/14, Change 9 Jul 22)

sections.title: INTRODUCTION (CHAPTER 4 - TAKEOFF, CLIMB, AND LEVEL-OFF)
sections.technique_summary: This phase of flight is very dynamic and can be as complicated as any other part of the mission. Complex departure procedures may be required immediately after takeoff in the low altitude environment, and communications can be very busy leaving the terminal area. Emergency situations, when they occur in this phase of flight, require forethought, and quick correct action. Solid preparation is essential to success.
sections.notes: Chapter opener; no gradable item mapping. Printed page 47 = PDF page 57 (offset +10, not +8).

sections.title: LINEUP CHECK
sections.technique_summary: Objective is to accomplish checklist items in preparation for takeoff. This check is normally accomplished after you have stopped the A/C on the center line of the active runway. The PF must ensure that all items are complete and "BOTH" items are confirmed with the PNF. Clear final prior to crossing the runway hold short line.

parameters.name: NWS (lineup check item N)
parameters.value: Deselect after A/C aligned with RWY
parameters.verbatim: N — NWS: Deselect NWS after the A/C is aligned with the RWY

parameters.name: IFF transponder (lineup check item I)
parameters.verbatim: I — IFF transponder: NORMAL

parameters.name: Landing Light (lineup check item L)
parameters.verbatim: L — Landing Light: ON

parameters.name: Taxi Light (lineup check item T)
parameters.verbatim: T — Taxi Light: ON

parameters.name: ANTICE (lineup check item A)
parameters.verbatim: A — ANTICE: ON

parameters.name: Panel Clear (lineup check item P)
parameters.verbatim: P — Panel Clear (Only ANTI ICE is ON)

procedure_steps: Stop the A/C on the center line of the active runway.
Clear final prior to crossing the runway hold short line.
PF ensures all items are complete; "BOTH" items are confirmed with the PNF.
Run the NILTAP acronym: NWS deselect, IFF NORMAL, Landing Light ON, Taxi Light ON, ANTICE ON, Panel Clear (only ANTI ICE ON).
sections.notes: The manual gives NILTAP explicitly as "a common technique to remember the checklist steps". No common-errors block is published for this paragraph.

sections.title: TAKEOFF
sections.technique_summary: Objective is to safely get the A/C airborne. Two takeoff options exist, static and rolling. The static takeoff is used early in training because it provides more time to accomplish required checks and verify proper engine operation; a static takeoff is also required at night and for solo students. A rolling takeoff aids traffic flow in a busy pattern and is a smooth transition from taxi to takeoff roll. Rolling takeoffs have a negligible effect on TOLD and no recalculation is required.

parameters.name: engine runup torque (static takeoff)
parameters.verbatim: Clear down the runway and advance the PCL to 25 to 30 % torque.

parameters.name: power for takeoff roll
parameters.verbatim: release brakes to begin the takeoff roll and smoothly advance PCL to MAX

parameters.name: engine instrument check timing at max power
parameters.value: approximately 3 seconds after PCL reaches MAX
parameters.verbatim: Check engine instruments when stabilized at maximum power (approximately 3 seconds after PCL reaches MAX) to ensure proper operation.

parameters.name: elevator position during takeoff roll
parameters.verbatim: Position the elevator approximately neutral to prevent the nose gear from digging in during takeoff roll.

parameters.name: takeoff attitude
parameters.verbatim: smoothly apply backstick pressure to establish the takeoff attitude (approximately 7° to 10° nose high, Figure 4.1.)

parameters.name: rotation speed (no gusts)
parameters.verbatim: Without wind gusts, rotation speed is 85 KIAS.

parameters.name: rotation speed correction for gusty winds
parameters.value: increase by 1/2 the gust factor, up to 10 knot increase
parameters.verbatim: If gusty winds are present, increase rotation speed by 1/2 the gust factor (up to 10 knot increase).

procedure_steps: Check the windsock and take note of winds reported by the RSU or tower controller.
Anticipate takeoff clearance by listening to the position reports of other A/C in the pattern.
When cleared for line-up, slowly taxi to align the A/C with the runway centerline, come to a complete stop and execute the lineup check.

Static takeoff: stop aligned with the runway; pump up the brakes to prevent creep during engine runup; PNF guards the brakes (without touching rudder pedals), ready to assume control; clear down the runway and advance PCL to 25 to 30 % torque; crosscheck outside to detect creep and check engine instruments; when cleared for takeoff release brakes and smoothly advance PCL to MAX; check engine instruments when stabilized at maximum power.
Rolling takeoff: once aligned with the runway, disengage NWS and smoothly advance the PCL to MAX; check engine instruments when stabilized at maximum power.
Takeoff roll: with no crosswind, deflect the control stick slightly right to compensate for torque at MAX power; with a crosswind, deflect the control stick into the crosswind component.
Position the elevator approximately neutral; counteract the left deviation with right rudder.
Move the heels from the rudder pedals to the floor and use rudder for directional control throughout the takeoff roll.
At rotation speed (85 KIAS without gusts) smoothly apply backstick pressure to establish approximately 7° to 10° nose high.
Immediately after takeoff and safe gear retraction, apply some right rudder trim to counteract adverse yaw and center the ball.
common_errors: Making a radio call while an A/C is landing or taking off ("Do not to make a radio call while an A/C is landing or takeoff.").
A/C creep during engine runup if the brakes are not pumped up — crosscheck outside to detect creep.
Failing to deflect the control stick slightly right without crosswind, so torque generated at MAX power is not compensated.
Failing to deflect the control stick into the crosswind component, allowing the upwind wing to lift.
Elevator not approximately neutral, so the nose gear digs in during takeoff roll.
Not counteracting the A/C tendency to deviate to the left caused by power application (insufficient right rudder).
Leaving the heels on the rudder pedals, risking accidental brake application.
Using control inputs that are too large as airspeed increases — flight controls become more effective, so progressively smaller inputs are required.
Not applying right rudder trim after takeoff/safe gear retraction, leaving adverse yaw and the ball off center.
corrections: Counteract the left deviation from power application by applying right rudder.
Move the heels from the rudder pedals to the floor to prevent accidental brake application and use rudder for directional control throughout the takeoff roll.
Progressively use smaller control inputs as airspeed increases to maintain A/C control.
Technique: reduce the pitch attitude picture by half (place the spinner slightly below the horizon) to attain the takeoff attitude; use control stick pressure as necessary to hold this attitude.
Immediately after takeoff and safe gear retraction apply some right rudder trim to counteract adverse yaw and center the ball.
sections.notes: Figure 4.1 (PDF page 59) is titled "FCP Takeoff Pitch Attitude" and is image-only — no extractable numeric text beyond the 7°–10° in the body.

sections.title: CROSSWIND TAKEOFF
sections.technique_summary: The procedures for a takeoff with a crosswind are the same as for a no wind takeoff except aileron is held into the wind to keep the wings level. Aileron deflection is necessary because the upwind wing develops more lift, causing it to fly (begin rising) before the downwind wing. Anticipate the aileron requirement due to the crosswind and either preposition aileron into the wind or apply aileron into wind as required during takeoff roll. Use rudder to keep the A/C from weather-vaning.
procedure_steps: Use the same procedures as a no wind takeoff.
Hold aileron into the wind to keep the wings level.
Anticipate the aileron requirement: either preposition aileron into the wind or apply aileron into wind as required during takeoff roll.
Use rudder to keep the A/C from weather-vaning (for example, crabbing or turning into the wind).
Use progressively smaller control inputs as airspeed increases.
common_errors: Insufficient aileron into the wind, allowing the upwind wing to rise — "If the upwind wing rises skipping may result (Figure 4.2.)."

Skipping: "a series of very small bounces caused when the A/C attempts to fly on one wing and settles back onto the runway. During these bounces, the A/C moves sideways and stress on the landing gear is increased."
Allowing the A/C to weather-vane (for example, crabbing or turning into the wind) instead of holding runway alignment with rudder.
Failing to reduce control input size as airspeed increases (controls become more effective).
corrections: Anticipate aileron requirement due to the crosswind and either preposition aileron into the wind or apply aileron into wind as required during takeoff roll.
Use rudder to keep the A/C from weather-vaning.
Progressively smaller control inputs are required to maintain A/C control as airspeed increases.
sections.notes: Figure 4.2 "Skipping on Takeoff" is on PDF page 60 (printed 50) and is image-only.

sections.title: AFTER BECOMING AIRBORNE
sections.technique_summary: Objective is to transition the A/C from takeoff roll to climb. Control inputs change significantly as the A/C leaves the ground; rudder requirements change as the wheels leave the ground and airspeed increases. Retract gear and flaps when safely airborne with a positive climb rate and engine instruments are checked within limits. Gear and flap retraction should be a conscious, deliberate act.

parameters.name: climb airspeed after airborne
parameters.verbatim: a. Airspeed – Accelerate to climb airspeed (140-180 KIAS)

parameters.name: power after airborne
parameters.verbatim: b. Power – Max

parameters.name: pitch after airborne
parameters.verbatim: c. Pitch – As required to fly desired airspeed (normally 10-15°)

parameters.name: landing gear and flap airspeed limit
parameters.verbatim: confirm the landing gear warning lights are extinguished and the flaps are up before the landing gear and flap airspeed limit of 147KIAS

parameters.name: maximum climb rate airspeed / pitch
parameters.value: 140 KIAS, nose as high as 12° above the horizon
parameters.verbatim: Although the maximum climb rate occurs at 140 KIAS with the nose as high as 12° above the horizon

parameters.name: normal climb-out airspeed
parameters.verbatim: normally accelerate to 16 0-180 KIAS during climb out to allow the nose to be lower to improve forward visibility

procedure_steps: Retract gear and flaps when safely airborne with a positive climb rate and engine instruments checked within limits.
Before moving the gear handle, the PF makes an intercockpit "gear clear" / gear up call and pauses momentarily.
On student presolo contact sorties the IP must acknowledge the "gear clear" call with "clear" before the student pilot raises the gear; on all other sorties "gear clear" is an advisory call only.
After gear and flap retraction, confirm the landing gear warning lights are extinguished and the flaps are up before 147 KIAS.
Check that the engine instruments are within limits.
As airspeed increases, apply nose-down trim to relieve pressure on the control stick.
Technique: PF verbalizes "climbing, good engine, gear clear" prior to raising the gear and flaps; PNF may respond "clear" once verifying safely airborne and climbing.
Verify climbing by altimeter and VSI indications; monitor torque and ITT within tolerances.

Technique for cleanup confirmation: PF says "Gear and flaps up at (read airspeed) below 147 KIAS" — gear up: gear handle light, three green and three red lights are all out; flaps up: check the flap gauge; airspeed: read directly from the airspeed indicator after the flap gauge is crosschecked.
common_errors: Raising gear/flaps without a positive climb rate or before engine instruments are checked within limits — "Gear and flap retraction should be a conscious, deliberate act."
Moving the gear handle without the intercockpit "gear clear" call and momentary pause.
On student presolo contact sorties, the student raising the gear before the IP acknowledges "gear clear" with "clear".
Failing to confirm gear warning lights extinguished and flaps up before the 147 KIAS gear/flap airspeed limit.
Not applying nose-down trim as airspeed increases, leaving pressure on the control stick.
Climbing at maximum-rate pitch (nose as high as 12°) so that forward visibility is restricted, instead of accelerating to the normal 160-180 KIAS climb-out.
corrections: As airspeed increases, apply nose-down trim to relieve pressure on the control stick.
Normally accelerate to 160-180 KIAS during climb out to allow the nose to be lower and improve forward visibility.
Verbally confirm the A/C is cleaned up by gear/flap limiting airspeed.
sections.notes: The source text renders the normal climb-out speed as "16 0-180 KIAS" (extraction artifact of 160-180 KIAS); verbatim preserved as printed.

sections.title: AFTER BECOMING AIRBORNE (CROSSWIND)
sections.technique_summary: Control inputs change significantly as the A/C leaves the ground. Crosswind controls must be released after takeoff, as the A/C is allowed to crab into the wind, to prevent the upwind wing from dipping towards the ground. Rudder requirements change as the wheels leave the ground, airspeed increases, and the A/C crabs into the wind. Climb in coordinated flight and maintain runway alignment on takeoff leg.
procedure_steps: Release the crosswind controls after takeoff.
Allow the A/C to crab into the wind.
Adjust rudder as the wheels leave the ground, airspeed increases and the A/C crabs into the wind.
Climb in coordinated flight and maintain runway alignment on takeoff leg.
common_errors: Holding crosswind controls after takeoff instead of releasing them, so the upwind wing dips towards the ground.
Not climbing in coordinated flight / failing to maintain runway alignment on takeoff leg.
corrections: Crosswind controls must be released after takeoff and the A/C allowed to crab into the wind, to prevent the upwind wing from dipping towards the ground.
Climb in coordinated flight and maintain runway alignment on takeoff leg.
sections.notes: Figure 4.3 "Crabbing Into Crosswind After Takeoff" is on PDF page 61 (printed 51) and is image-only.

sections.title: ABNORMAL PROCEDURES — TAKEOFF ABORTS
sections.technique_summary: If there is reason to ABORT the takeoff, do not hesitate to do so. If the PNF sees something hazardous should inform the PF. If the A/C Commander (AC) is not flying during a time-critical situation that requires immediate action, and there is no time to relay this to the PF, the AC should take control of the A/C and accomplish the appropriate procedures.
procedure_steps: If there is reason to ABORT the takeoff, do not hesitate to do so.
PNF informs the PF upon seeing something hazardous.

If the AC is not flying during a time-critical situation requiring immediate action and there is no time to relay it to the PF, the AC takes control of the A/C and accomplishes the appropriate procedures.
common_errors: Hesitating to abort when there is reason to ABORT the takeoff.
PNF failing to inform the PF after seeing something hazardous.
corrections: Do not hesitate to abort when there is reason to.
In a time-critical situation with no time to relay to the PF, the A/C Commander takes control and accomplishes the appropriate procedures.

sections.title: ABNORMAL PROCEDURES — WAKE TURBULENCE
sections.technique_summary: Anticipate wake turbulence when taking off behind other A/C on the same or parallel runways, especially if the wind is calm or straight down the runway. Wake turbulence is formed when an A/C is creating lift, therefore plan to take off at a point prior to the preceding A/C's take-off point or after their point of touchdown.
procedure_steps: Anticipate wake turbulence when taking off behind other A/C on the same or parallel runways, especially if the wind is calm or straight down the runway.
Plan to take off at a point prior to the preceding A/C's take-off point, or after their point of touchdown.
common_errors: Failing to anticipate wake turbulence when taking off behind other A/C on the same or parallel runways, especially with calm wind or wind straight down the runway.
Taking off past the preceding A/C's take-off point (and before their point of touchdown), i.e. into the wake.
corrections: Plan to take off at a point prior to the preceding A/C's take-off point or after their point of touchdown.

sections.title: TURNS AFTER TAKEOFF
sections.technique_summary: Climb straight ahead until past the departure end of the runway (or as directed). Attain a minimum of 140 KIAS and 700 feet AGL (local directives) before the first turn after takeoff.

parameters.name: minimum airspeed before first turn after takeoff
parameters.verbatim: Attain a minimum of 140 KIAS and 700 feet AGL (local directives) before the first turn after takeoff.

parameters.name: minimum altitude before first turn after takeoff
parameters.verbatim: Attain a minimum of 140 KIAS and 700 feet AGL (local directives) before the first turn after takeoff.

procedure_steps: Climb straight ahead until past the departure end of the runway (or as directed).
Attain a minimum of 140 KIAS and 700 feet AGL before the first turn after takeoff.
common_errors: Turning before passing the departure end of the runway (or before directed).
Turning below the minimum 140 KIAS and/or below 700 feet AGL.

sections.title: CLIMBS (INCLUDING CLIMBING TURNS AND LEVEL-OFF)
sections.technique_summary: Objective is to establish the A/C in a climb as required by local directives or published departure. Accelerate to climb airspeed 140-180 KIAS in accordance with local directives, power as required (normally MAX), pitch as required to fly the desired airspeed (normally 10-15°). Climbout airspeeds below 160 KIAS are permitted by the flight manual, but not normally recommended due to high pitch attitudes that limit forward visibility. Initiate the climb check in accordance with the flight manual passing 10.000 feet MSL.

parameters.name: climb airspeed
parameters.verbatim: a. Airspeed – Accelerate to climb airspeed 140-180 KIAS in accordance with local directives

parameters.name: climb power
parameters.verbatim: b. Power – As required, normally MAX

parameters.name: climb pitch
parameters.verbatim: c. Pitch – As required to fly desired airspeed (normally 10-15°)

parameters.name: minimum recommended climbout airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Climbout airspeeds below 160 KIAS are permitted by the flight manual, but not normally recommended due to high pitch attitudes that limit forward visibility.

parameters.name: climb check altitude
parameters.verbatim: Initiate the climb check in accordance with the flight manual passing 10.000 feet MSL.

parameters.name: climb gradient for 10° nose-high
parameters.value: approximately 1000 feet per nautical mile (1:1 ratio)
parameters.verbatim: A climb attitude of 10° nose-high results in a climb gradient of approximately 1000 feet per nautical mile (or what is referred to as a 1:1 ratio).

parameters.name: climb gradient rule of thumb
parameters.verbatim: This climb gradient is determined by using the formula that 1 degree is equal to 100 feet per nautical mile.

parameters.name: level flight pitch attitude at 160 KIAS
parameters.verbatim: Level flight for 160 KIAS is about 2-3° nose-high.

parameters.name: level-off lead point
parameters.value: approximately 10 % of the VSI (e.g. 200 feet below at 2.000 fpm)
parameters.verbatim: One technique is to use a lead point that is approximately 10 % of the VSI. For example, if climbing at a rate of 2.000 fpm, start the level-off 200 feet below the desired altitude.

procedure_steps: Accelerate to climb airspeed 140-180 KIAS in accordance with local directives; power as required, normally MAX; pitch as required to fly the desired airspeed (normally 10-15°).
Initiate the climb check in accordance with the flight manual passing 10.000 feet MSL.

Straight climb from level flight: advance PCL and increase A/C pitch; if above the desired climb speed, initially set the pitch to achieve the desired airspeed; after reaching the desired airspeed, lower the nose to keep airspeed constant as altitude increases.
Make all pitch changes using outside references when available.
Maintain heading using section lines, a prominent point or object near the horizon, or other outside references crosschecked with the heading on the EHSI.
Maintain wings-level attitude by outside references crosschecked with the attitude indicator.
Trim after power is set and the climbing attitude is established; trimming is a continuous process throughout the climb and level off.

Climbing turns: if standard bank angles are not required to comply with published routings, use shallow-banked turns to maintain a higher rate of climb; trim used in the turn must be taken out during the rollout.

Level-off: start the level-off at a lead point that allows a smooth transition to the desired level-off altitude (technique: approximately 10 % of the VSI); at the lead point smoothly lower the nose to level flight; approaching the desired airspeed adjust the PCL to obtain the desired airspeed and trim the A/C.
Conduct an operations check (OPS check) at initial level-off and periodically throughout the flight, according to the flight manual.
common_errors: Climbing out below 160 KIAS: permitted by the flight manual, but not normally recommended due to high pitch attitudes that limit forward visibility.
Failing to lower the nose after reaching the desired airspeed, so airspeed does not stay constant as altitude increases.
Making pitch changes on instruments instead of outside references when outside references are available.
Not trimming after power is set and the climbing attitude is established — trimming is a continuous process throughout the climb and level off.
Failing to take out the trim used in a climbing turn during the rollout.
Using standard/steeper bank angles when not required by published routings, reducing rate of climb.
Starting the level-off without an adequate lead point, so the transition to the level-off altitude is not smooth.
Omitting the operations check at initial level-off and periodically throughout the flight.
corrections: If above the desired climb speed, initially set the pitch to achieve the desired airspeed; after reaching the desired airspeed, lower the nose to keep airspeed constant as altitude increases.
Crosscheck heading on the EHSI against outside references; crosscheck wings level against the attitude indicator.
Trim used in the turn must be taken out during the rollout.
Use a level-off lead point of approximately 10 % of the VSI; at the lead point smoothly lower the nose to level flight, then adjust PCL to the desired airspeed and trim.
